Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our approach accurately models end-to-end latency and surpasses prior art in both estimation precision computational efficiency.

For intricate shapes, discretization using unstructured meshes is standard; however, evaluating potentials directly on these meshes via quadrature is often prohibitively expensive. This paper introduces a straightforward, high-order algorithm for calculating such potentials by utilizing Green's third identity to convert volume integrals into boundary integrals that are well-suited for the Helsing-Ojala method. Consequently, the processing time required for traditionally computationally intensive nearfield evaluations is balanced to match the handling of farfield interactions and other frontend tasks, all without incurring additional overhead beyond standard unstructured mesh operations. A comprehensive set of numerical experiments confirms the method's high-order accuracy and efficiency.
